sentences.text: This predator featured a skull roughly 16 centimeters long, equipped with massive lower jawbones that had double prongs and serrated edges for catching fish.
Its type species, Hadrosteus rapax, carries a name meaning "Rapacious Strong-Bone".
Gross first described the genus in 1932 based on fossils recovered from the Kellwasserkalk facies near Bad Wildungen, Germany.
Taxonomically, it belongs to the family Hadrosteidae within the clade Aspinothoracidi, which is part of the larger group Pachyosteomorphi.
It lived during the Frasnian stage of the Late Devonian period, existing between 382.31 and 372.15 million years ago.
